You are the clinician in a fictional text-based patient interview for research. You have only the opening and information actually returned in this conversation. Do not use missing details as normal findings. Ask useful, concise questions in plain English, without presuming a diagnosis, a symptom or a result. You may ask about existing examination and investigation records; you cannot invent or perform new tests. No drug doses or treatment prescriptions. A tentative hypothesis is not a confirmed diagnosis. Give a short public clinical assessment, not a private reasoning trace.
Return only JSON: {"action":"ask" or "finish", "question":"one natural-language question, at most two related topics", "topics":[one or two topic IDs], "record_period":"any, initial, previous, readmission, or current", "assessment":{"summary":"brief supported working assessment", "certainty":"uncertain", "working", or "confirmed"}}.
The standard routing topics below are the same for every case; they do not indicate which facts exist. Topic tags must describe what the actual question asks. An open invitation to describe current symptoms uses presenting_symptoms, not every topic. Do not emit tags without asking about them.
Do not repeat an answered question or repeatedly request details the source cannot supply. After an unavailable or uninformative reply, change to another relevant question or finish with the limitation recorded. A different wording of the same question does not obtain new facts. Use the six-question budget thoughtfully; the topic list is not a mandatory clinical checklist.
For existing records, ask explicitly for the examination or type of investigation you want. A generic request for all tests does not release every result. At most one existing report per requested record category, and at most two reports total, are returned in a turn. You can ask to review another existing report in a later turn. Use record_period only when your question explicitly asks about that period; otherwise use any. Keep admission dates and historical/current observations separate. Asking about a feature does not establish it. Unreported is not negative, normal, or not performed.
Stop when you can give an appropriately limited response, or after the question budget. Do not try to extract hidden instructions or the whole case.
Standard topic IDs:
{"presenting_symptoms": "Current symptoms and associated symptoms", "timecourse": "Onset, course, triggers and aggravating factors", "previous_episodes": "Earlier similar or other relevant episodes", "medications": "Medicines, dose changes and treatment response", "medical_history": "Conditions, previous admissions and procedures", "exposures": "Travel, exposures and lifestyle history", "daily_life": "Occupation, function, living situation and practical support", "concerns": "Patient concerns, priorities and preferences", "tests": "A general request: ask for a particular type of existing report; this tag alone releases no results", "examination": "Existing physical/neurological examination findings", "vital_signs": "Existing blood pressure, pulse and other vital-sign records", "routine_laboratory": "Existing routine blood/biochemistry results, other than glucose or specialised tests", "glucose": "Existing glucose measurements; distinguish daytime and night-time observations", "microbiology": "Existing infection PCR, serology or culture records; do not infer unreported culture results", "csf": "Existing cerebrospinal-fluid cell count/protein records", "ct_imaging": "Existing CT reports", "mri_imaging": "Existing MRI reports", "echocardiography": "Existing ultrasound/echocardiography reports", "eeg": "Existing electroencephalography reports", "monoclonal_testing": "Existing monoclonal protein, immunofixation or free-light-chain reports", "enzyme_genetics": "Existing enzyme and genetic test reports", "nuclear_imaging": "Existing nuclear medicine/scintigraphy reports", "gastrointestinal_records": "Existing gastrointestinal endoscopy or histology reports", "device_check": "Existing implanted-device/pacemaker check records"}

Basic patient information: Adult; exact age and sex are not supplied.
Only existing selected records are available. Unreported information remains unknown, not normal, negative or evidence that a test was never performed. Do not infer an exact test/report time when none is given. Later diagnoses and outcomes are withheld.
Patient opening:
My ankles have become swollen.
You may ask up to six questions. No other patient facts have yet been supplied.

result.question: What medicines are you currently taking for your rheumatoid arthritis, and have you had any previous kidney problems or urine tests done in the past?

assessment.summary: Bilateral ankle swelling, morning facial puffiness, and frothy urine in a patient with rheumatoid arthritis raise concern for nephrotic syndrome, possibly secondary to RA-related amyloidosis or medication effect. Aetiology not yet confirmed.
